time_plan.30m: Check whether Polymarket move is corroborated by any newswire (Reuters/Bloomberg/Caixin) or is isolated. Check FXI/ASHR pre-market or intraday tape and volume spike.
time_plan.1h: Compare FXI move to broad EM (EEM) to isolate China-specific risk versus global risk-off. Watch HK futures (HSI) and A-share overnight.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether official Chinese state media denies or stays silent; silence sustains risk premium. Re-check option skew on FXI.
time_plan.6h: Evaluate whether move has reversed (noise) or held/extended (real signal). Look for PBoC/SAFE stabilization signals or capital-control chatter.
time_plan.12h: Mark final FXI return vs entry; confirm whether any public confirmation emerged. If no corroboration and price reverted, log as false positive.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp upward move in the implied probability of Xi being removed before 2027 would signal acute elite political instability in China. Abrupt, non-orderly leadership transitions are a tail risk markets price as highly negative in the short term: policy uncertainty, capital flight risk, and a governance vacuum. US-listed China proxies like FXI are the most liquid vehicles to express this and would gap lower on credible leakage. Note the sign is short-term risk-off; a longer-term reassessment (e.g. hopes of less confrontational Taiwan posture) could partially offset, hence wide interval.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check USD/CNH offshore spot for a spike (more sensitive than CYB), and any PBoC fixing guidance.
time_plan.1h: Compare CNH move to DXY to separate China-specific stress from broad dollar strength.
time_plan.2h: Watch for PBoC intervention signals (state bank USD selling, fixing stronger than model).
time_plan.6h: Assess whether depreciation held despite likely official pushback.
time_plan.12h: Mark CNH/CYB level; note that heavy management likely muted any move regardless of the political signal.

predictions.reasoning: Political instability at the top of the CCP would pressure the yuan via capital-flight risk and uncertainty premium, though the PBoC manages the currency tightly and would lean against disorderly depreciation, capping the move. CYB is a liquid but low-volatility proxy, so expected magnitude is well below the 700bps tradable threshold — included as a corroborating signal rather than a standalone trade.

evidence_used: Market question implies a discrete, high-impact political regime event (Xi removal) in the world's second-largest economy
Primary topic tagged trade_policy, region china_taiwan — leadership change would carry large cross-asset spillovers
Liquid US-listed China proxies (FXI, ASHR, KWEB) and managed CNH are the standard channels for pricing China political risk
uncertainty_notes: Base rate of Xi actually being removed is very low; most probability moves in this market are likely noise or thin-liquidity swings, not information
Direction is genuinely ambiguous over longer horizons — a leadership change could be read as reducing Taiwan-conflict risk, which is equity-positive
PBoC tight management means FX proxy will underreact relative to the underlying stress
Polymarket on Chinese internal politics is especially prone to rumor-driven spikes with no verifiable source

llm_justification.summary: If the implied probability of Xi Jinping being removed before 2027 spikes sharply, the cleanest public-market read is acute short-term China political-instability risk-off: liquid China equity proxies (FXI) fall and the offshore yuan weakens. The equity channel is the only one with plausible >700bps magnitude, and even that carries high uncertainty because the underlying event is a low-base-rate tail and the directional sign could flip on longer-horizon reassessment. The FX proxy is included as corroboration but is structurally muted by PBoC management.
key_assumptions: A sharp move in this market reflects leaked/early information rather than pure noise
Markets price abrupt CCP leadership change as near-term negative for Chinese risk assets
FXI and CYB remain liquid and tradeable within the 12h window
failure_modes: The probability move is thin-market noise with no underlying event, and prices mean-revert within hours (false positive)
Information was already public/discounted, so no residual asset move occurs
Longer-term interpretation flips sign — removal seen as de-risking Taiwan, lifting China equities instead of depressing them
CNH proxy barely moves due to heavy PBoC management, making the FX leg uninformative
FXI move is driven by unrelated global risk-off (EM-wide), not China-specific political signal
